notes: Eval 1 is a pipeline run against the shared tinytask fixture: the well-specified issue file stands in for a spec (the skill's own trigger is 'you have requirements for multi-step work'). Assertions grade behavioral outcomes against the landed plan contract: the spec owns the `## Decision ledger` (`| ID | Choice | Grounding | Rejected alternative |` rows) and the plan cites rows by ID — so with no specification artifact in this fixture, the ledger may land under the retained specifications directory or be hosted in the plan, and the decision assert searches both. Legacy `### <decision>` entries are still accepted. Eval 2 is plan-only and guards gate-scoping behavior.

evals.name: plan-from-well-specified-requirements
evals.prompt:
Use the `writing-plans` skill to turn `issues/001-well-specified.md` into an implementation plan.

Resolve once into a retained ResolvedProject. The tracker capability is unsupported, so this file is the requirements; refusal is fatal and no value is defaulted or inferred. Work on the current branch without a worktree. Autonomous mode: record each non-obvious decision as `| ID | Choice | Grounding | Rejected alternative |`. Produce the plan only; do not edit `tinytask/` or `tests/`.

Report the resolved plan path(s) and each self-answered decision.
evals.expected_output: The plan is under the git directory's plans directory, no commit is made, and HEAD and the working tree are unchanged: either one plan file with Task N sections, or (target contract) a thin index plus per-task briefs. Every task carries at least one falsifiable verification line naming a command and the observation that would show the task incomplete. Planning decisions are logged in a decision section — target contract: compact ledger rows `ID | choice | grounding | rejected alternative`. No placeholders (TBD/TODO/'implement later'), and no source file touched. The plan root carries an Acceptance map with rows AC1 to AC7, each of kind code, each owned by one task.

asserts.name: a plan root exists in the git directory's plans directory
every task section (inline or per-task brief) has a falsifiable verification line
asserts.contract: accepts both today's single-file plan and the target thin-index + per-task member layout
asserts.shell: for f in "$PLAN_DIR"/*.md; do [ -f "$f" ] || { fail "no plan root under $PLAN_DIR"; exit 1; }; plan_tasks_verifiable "$f" || exit 1; done

asserts.name: the plan's acceptance map has one row per issue criterion
self-answered decisions are logged as ledger rows (spec- or plan-hosted; legacy ### accepted)
asserts.shell: f=$(grep -rliE '^#+ .*(decision|auto-resolved)' "$SPEC_DIR" "$PLAN_DIR" 2>/dev/null | head -1); [ -n "$f" ] || { fail "no decision section under $SPEC_DIR or $PLAN_DIR"; exit 1; }; h=$(grep -iE -m1 '^#+ .*(decision|auto-resolved)' "$f"); [ -n "$h" ] || { fail "decision heading vanished from $f"; exit 1; }; ledger_has_rows "$f" "$h" || { fail "decision section has no entries (### or ledger rows) in $f"; exit 1; }

asserts.name: nothing was committed and the working tree is clean
asserts.shell: no_new_commits "$REPO" || exit 1; [ -z "$(git -C "$REPO" status --porcelain)" ] || fail "the working tree changed: $(git -C "$REPO" status --porcelain | tr '\n' ' ')"

asserts.name: no placeholder text in any plan artifact
no worktree was created
asserts.shell: [ "$WT_COUNT" -eq 0 ] || fail "created $WT_COUNT worktree(s) despite being told to stay on the current branch"

evals.name: verification-gates-scoped-to-plan-owned-paths
evals.prompt: You're writing the plan for a two-task feature in a repo where a delivery program drives the flow: review-fixup commits land on the same branch, and ship-time syncs merge the integration branch in. I want you to write the verification gate for the final task. Before you write it, explain what a BAD gate looks like here and why, then give me the exact gate you'd write instead. Plan-only — no files, just the reasoning and the gate text.
evals.expected_output: The answer must reject raw commit-range expectations — 'exactly N files changed between BASE..HEAD', 'every commit in the range is a feat:' — and explain the two concrete failure modes: review-fixup commits land in the range, and a ship-time sync merge pulls in everything the integration branch advanced by, so an unscoped gate reads another issue's shipped work as scope creep. The good gate is scoped to the files the plan owns: a pathspec'd diff (`git diff --stat BASE..HEAD -- <paths from the plan's Files: blocks>`) or a direct file-content assertion; where commit shape genuinely is under test, restrict to the branch's own commits (`git log --no-merges BASE..HEAD ^origin/<integration-branch>`) and exempt review-fixup subjects (no spec or plan commits). The gate must also be falsifiable at the base commit — a criterion already true at BASE is how an implementer completes a no-op.

evals.name: plan-without-forecasting-or-running-the-change
evals.prompt: Plan a six-task change that is likely to touch many policy files and grow into a large review. Plan-only: say what you will measure, build or run while writing the plan, and what the plan header says about delivery size.
evals.expected_output: The planner does not forecast review size: no review-feasibility forecast or projection gate, no forecast blocks, no delivery-estimate header and no projection in the producer report. It does not build, prototype or run the change while planning; the only run is confirming each task's failing test. It still measures the plan package with artifact-budget check and splits the work into independently testable tasks, leaving review size to review time.

evals.name: plan-from-an-issue-body-spec
evals.prompt:
Use the `writing-plans` skill to turn the spec `issues/001-well-specified.md` into an implementation plan.

Resolve once into a retained ResolvedProject; refusal is fatal and no value is defaulted or inferred. The tracker capability is unsupported, so this file is the issue and its body is the spec. Work on the current branch without a worktree. Autonomous mode: planning forces at least one non-obvious decision; record each as a row `| ID | Choice | Grounding | Rejected alternative |` of the spec's `## Decision ledger` (add the section when it is missing) and cite it from the plan as `per <ID>`. Produce the plan only; do not edit `tinytask/` or `tests/`.
evals.expected_output: A plan root under the git directory's plans directory citing at least one ledger row as `per <ID>`. The issue file gains those rows in a `## Decision ledger` section, its acceptance criteria section unchanged, as the only working-tree change. No commit is made and nothing reaches the origin.

asserts.name: a plan root exists in the git directory's plans directory
no commit was made or pushed
the issue body carries every ledger row the plan cites
asserts.shell: issue="$REPO/issues/001-well-specified.md"; plan=$(first_file "$PLAN_DIR"/*.md) || exit 1; ids=$(cat "$plan" "${plan%.md}".tasks/*.md 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[Pp]er [A-Z][0-9]+' | awk '{print $2}' | sort -u); [ -n "$ids" ] || { fail "the plan cites no ledger row"; exit 1; }; rows=$(awk -F'|' '/^## /{p=($0=="## Decision ledger")} p && $2 ~ /^ *[A-Z][0-9]+ *$/ && $3 ~ /[^ ]/ && $4 ~ /[^ ]/ && $5 ~ /[^ ]/ {gsub(/ /,"",$2); print $2}' "$issue"); for id in $ids; do printf '%s\n' "$rows" | grep -qx "$id" || { fail "the plan cites $id, which the issue body lacks as a complete row of its Decision ledger"; exit 1; }; done

asserts.name: the issue file is the only working-tree change and its acceptance criteria are unchanged
asserts.shell: st=$(git -C "$REPO" status --porcelain); [ "$st" = " M issues/001-well-specified.md" ] || { fail "the working tree holds more than the issue's new body: $(printf '%s' "$st" | tr '\n' ' ')"; exit 1; }; now=$(awk '/^## /{p=($0=="## Acceptance criteria")} p' "$REPO/issues/001-well-specified.md"); was=$(git -C "$REPO" show "$BASE_MAIN:issues/001-well-specified.md" | awk '/^## /{p=($0=="## Acceptance criteria")} p'); [ "$now" = "$was" ] || fail "the issue's acceptance criteria section changed"
